claims.text: Unprotected conventional metal parts, such as carbon steel, rapidly degrade during prolonged exposure to high-temperature molten aluminum.
A thin Al2O3 ceramic coating can be deposited on equipment parts by physical vapor deposition.
The proposed Al2O3 coating is stable at the operating temperatures of hot-dip aluminum plating.
An optimized Al2O3 coating can act as an impermeable physical barrier.
An optimized Al2O3 coating can act as a chemical barrier against molten aluminum.
The Al2O3 coating prevents direct contact between molten aluminum and the underlying metal substrate.
Isolation of the molten aluminum from the metal substrate reduces reactions at their interface.
Reducing direct contact and interfacial reactions decreases corrosion of the substrate.
The Al2O3 coating reduces mechanical degradation or erosion caused during molten-aluminum exposure.
Al2O3-coated parts will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than uncoated parts under identical operating conditions.
Al2O3-coated parts will have a significantly lower erosion rate than uncoated parts under identical operating conditions.
Reduced corrosion and erosion will extend the service life of coated equipment parts relative to uncoated parts.
Protection depends on the coating remaining intact and free from cracking and delamination during thermal cycling and mechanical loading.
Coating failure or extreme operating variations can reduce the coating's protective effect.
